comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: broken require path — the module cannot be loaded**

`js/common/bugFixBatchContext.js:10` requires `./configLoader.js`:

```javascript
var configLoader = require('./configLoader.js');
```

But `configLoader.js` lives at `js/configLoader.js` — one directory **up**. From inside `js/common/`, `./configLoader.js` resolves to the nonexistent `js/common/configLoader.js`. Verified directly: `node -e "require('./js/common/bugFixBatchContext.js')"` fails with `Cannot find module './configLoader.js'`.

This is not cosmetic — per the gh-823 rule in AGENTS.md, top-level (load-time) requires resolve **file-relative**, and `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. So this breaks:

1. **Runtime**: `js/prepareBugFixBatchContext.js:17` and `js/developBugFixBatchAndCreatePR.js` both `require('./common/bugFixBatchContext.js')` — the bug-fix-batch pre/post actions will fail at module load ("Failed to require module") in the GraalJS engine.
2. **Pack build**: `dmtools compile` will fail to close the pack over a nonexistent file.

Every sibling module in `js/common/` uses the correct `../configLoader.js` (actionTicketContext.js:15, buildEncodedConfig.js:13, contentOutput.js:32, trackers.js:57, etc.) — this one slipped through because the unit tests load the module via `loadModule(..., makeRequire({ './configLoader.js': configLoaderMock, ... }))` (`js/unit-tests/test_developBugFixBatchAndCreatePR.js:51-56`), which maps the literal spec string and never exercises real path resolution.

Fix: `require('../configLoader.js')`. Ideally also wire `test_bugFixBatchDevelopment.js` into `run_all.json` (see the related IMPORTANT comment) so real path resolution gets exercised.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: payload key precedence silently changed for mergeBot's list normalization**

`main`'s `sm/mergeBot.js:listArray` (pre-PR, at `origin/main:js/sm/mergeBot.js:55`) resolved wrapped payloads as:

```javascript
return Array.isArray(prs) ? prs : (prs.pullRequests || prs.items || []);
```

The shared `common/mcpParse.js:payloadList` prefers the opposite order — `items` first, then `pullRequests`:

```javascript
if (parsed && Array.isArray(parsed.items)) return parsed.items;
if (parsed && Array.isArray(parsed.pullRequests)) return parsed.pullRequests;
```

For `mergeTrigger.js`'s original `asList` the new order is identical (it also checked `items` first), but for `mergeBot.js` any `github_list_prs` payload carrying **both** keys now yields `items` where it previously yielded `pullRequests`. If the bridge never emits both keys in one payload this is a no-op — but the docstring here ("the semantics are identical") is not accurate, and the merged-slot release path (gh-952) consumes this list.

Please confirm against the bridge's actual `github_list_prs` payload shape. If both keys can co-occur, keep `mergeBot`'s original precedence (e.g. a `preferPullRequests` flag on `payloadList`) or make the docstring state the deliberate unification.

comments.body:
📍 **`js/writeSolutionAndLabels.js:106`**

🚨 **BLOCKING: malformed markdown table separator — Confluence "Affected Repositories" section no longer parses as a table**

The refactor of `buildConfluenceMarkdownSection` changed the delimiter row from 4 columns to 2:

```javascript
lines.push('| # | Repository | Reason | Depends On |');
lines.push('|---|---|');   // was '|---|---|---|---|' on main
```

Per the GFM table spec, the header row must match the delimiter row in the number of cells — otherwise the table is **not recognized** and renders as raw pipe text. The other two formatters in this same file kept the correct 4-column delimiter (`buildMarkdownSection` at line 91), so this is a typo introduced by the extraction (commit `953b9130`), not an intentional format change — `origin/main:js/writeSolutionAndLabels.js:150` shows `|---|---|---|---|`.

This function is not dead code: `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js:142` calls it (via the lazy require) to append the Affected Repositories section to every published Confluence page, so the regression is user-visible on the Confluence publish path.

Fix: restore `lines.push('|---|---|---|---|');` — and please add a test asserting the Confluence section's separator, since `test_writeSolutionAndLabels.js` only covers the Jira/ADO sections today.
